# px0: Read Code. Fast.

> px0 is a fast, ultra-light, remote-first IDE designed for instant code navigation and review in your browser. Booting in under 1 ms and using ~20 MB of RAM, it turns your browser into a zero-latency inspection console with symbol-level navigation, deep search, git awareness, visual diffing, and agent edit dispatch.

## Positioning

Code now arrives from the terminal, not the keyboard. Whether generated by AI coding agents, executed in CI runners, or compiled on remote cloud VMs, developers spend less time manually authoring code and more time in review, audit, and navigation:

- Terminals drive generation: agents, compilers, and scripts write code, run tests, and manage workflows.
- Developers drive verification: inspecting git diffs, following symbol references, previewing documentation, browsing surrounding context, and auditing architecture.
- Traditional IDEs are overkill for this: booting an Electron app or a resource-intensive IDE suite just to inspect code costs gigabytes of memory and seconds of startup.
- Remote development has friction: standard remote setups require SSH keys, port forwarding tunnels, and heavy server-side daemons or remote desktop software.

px0 does the code viewing job exceptionally well: an instant, distraction-free environment to read, explore, diff, and verify code locally or remotely, with full LSP intelligence and search at near-zero overhead.

| Parameter | Traditional IDE (such as VS Code) | px0 |
| --------- | --------------------------------- | --- |
| Primary purpose | Manual code authoring and plugin host | Instant code reading, diffing, and navigation |
| Base memory (RSS) | ~1,440 MB | ~20 MB |
| Startup CPU spike | 35% - 50% | < 1% |
| Cold startup | Several seconds | Sub-millisecond |
| Process tree | 15+ Node.js / Electron processes | 1 static Go binary |
| Setup | Config files, plugins, node, npm | Zero config, zero runtime |
| Remote access | Heavy server daemons, SSH tunnels | Single HTTP/TLS port, zero daemon |

## Primary Use Cases

1. **Verifying AI Agent Output**: Trace symbol references, inspect live git diffs against HEAD, review generated code, and close the tab without leaving your terminal flow.
2. **Remote & Cloud Server Inspection**: Spin up on any remote server, VM, or CI runner and browse the codebase instantly from your local browser with zero SSH keys, zero port-forwarding hassle, and no heavy remote desktop daemons.
3. **Auditing Large Repositories**: Read through massive, 50,000+ file codebases (e.g. the Linux kernel with 95,710 files) on a laptop without background indexers hogging RAM or spinning up fans.
4. **Sidecar to Terminal Editors**: Keep lightweight editors (like Vim, Neovim, or Helix) in the terminal for typing, while using px0 as a high-density, rich graphical inspection and diff console.

## Features

- Fuzzy file search (Cmd/Ctrl+P), document symbols (Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+O), and full workspace text search (Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+F) in milliseconds. Full workspace search is integrated into a dedicated tab in the right inspector panel alongside symbols, references, and calls.
- Git awareness: working tree status badges (M, A, D, U, R) in the file tree, dirty ancestor directory bubbling so collapsed folders never hide edits, and a changed-only file filter toggle.
- Visual diff viewer: side-by-side split diff and unified diff against HEAD with line-level change gutters (Cmd/Ctrl+D).
- Rendered Markdown preview: goldmark GFM rendering with Chroma syntax-highlighted code fences, synchronized scroll position, and instant Preview/Source toggle (Alt+M).
- Syntax highlighting for ~280 languages via Chroma, lexed in bounded windows rather than whole files.
- 14 built-in themes: Tokyo Night (default), Paper, Catppuccin Latte, Catppuccin Mocha, Dracula, GitHub Dark, Gruvbox Dark, Gruvbox Light, Monokai, Nord, One Dark, Rose Pine, Solarized Dark, Solarized Light.
- Optional LSP: zero-config detection of gopls, rust-analyzer, pyright, ruff, typescript-language-server, clangd, zls, lua-language-server, and solargraph for go-to-definition (F12), hover, and references (Shift+F12). Falls back to regex outlines and inspector search when no server is installed.
- Virtualized rendering: opening a 400,000-line file costs the same as a 10-line file; only visible lines are in the DOM (~60 DOM rows mounted).
- Remote-friendly and self-contained: single static binary embedding HTML, CSS, and JS with zero runtime dependencies.
- Privacy-first: no code, file paths, or search queries leave your machine.
- Self-updating: `px0 --update`, plus an asynchronous daily check that never delays startup.

## Remote Sessions Architecture

px0 is built to inspect remote codebases as easily as local ones:

- **Zero SSH or heavy client setup**: Remote editors install gigabytes of Node runtimes and server daemons on the host machine. px0 runs as a single lightweight binary, serving directly over HTTP/TLS without requiring SSH shell sessions.
- **Single port over any wire**: Pass `-host 0.0.0.0` or `-port 7777` to bind the web console. Access from any browser on your laptop, iPad, or phone across your private VPN, Tailscale mesh, WireGuard, reverse proxy, or Cloudflare Tunnel with pooled gzip compression.
- **Sandboxed by architecture**: `safePath` rejects directory traversal attempts, host header checks protect against DNS rebinding, and external stdlib jumps require explicit LSP allowlisting. Agent editing endpoints are protected by origin verification.

Common setups:
- Dev box / cloud VM: `px0 -host 0.0.0.0 -port 7777 ~/work/repo` (access over private network / Tailscale)
- Headless CI / test runner: `px0 -no-open -port 8080 /workspace` (inspect failed build workspaces)
- Ephemeral Docker / container: `docker run -p 7777:7777 -v $(pwd):/src px0:latest` (browse isolated containers)

## Git Awareness & Diffing

px0 provides native Git working tree awareness designed specifically for reviewing changes:

- Status badges: files display clear indicators for modified (M), added (A), deleted (D), untracked (U), and renamed (R) paths.
- Ancestor propagation: when a deeply nested file changes, every parent directory receives an indicator dot. You never miss changes inside collapsed folders.
- Changed-only filter: one click prunes tens of thousands of clean files down to only the files touched in the working tree.
- Myers diff engine: in-memory diff calculation against HEAD without spawning external shell processes or locking index files.
- Split and unified views: side-by-side split layout and unified diff view with green added lines, red deleted lines, and full syntax highlighting preserved.

## Benchmarks

Measured on Linux with language servers disabled (`-no-lsp`), fastest of 5 requests, using `./benchmark.sh` on shallow clones.

| Repository | Source | Files | Index | Fuzzy | Full scan | Open big | Reopen | RSS | Peak |
| ---------- | ------ | ----- | ----- | ----- | --------- | -------- | ------ | --- | ---- |
| flask | 3 MB | 235 | 1 ms | 0.8 ms | 2.3 ms | n/a | n/a | 16 MB | 18 MB |
| redis | 26 MB | 1,855 | 13 ms | 1.0 ms | 18.2 ms | 80.8 ms | 1.2 ms | 17 MB | 27 MB |
| django | 74 MB | 7,014 | 39 ms | 1.3 ms | 26.8 ms | 166.8 ms | 1.0 ms | 20 MB | 29 MB |
| react | 63 MB | 7,178 | 52 ms | 2.7 ms | 32.2 ms | 57.7 ms | 0.7 ms | 21 MB | 28 MB |
| kubernetes | 370 MB | 25,926 | 150 ms | 13.5 ms | 84.6 ms | 199.0 ms | 0.9 ms | 30 MB | 44 MB |
| typescript | 414 MB | 66,533 | 566 ms | 6.2 ms | 150.3 ms | 40.9 ms | 6.5 ms | 69 MB | 105 MB |
| linux | 1,809 MB | 95,710 | 370 ms | 6.0 ms | 451.8 ms | 26.7 ms | 0.6 ms | 55 MB | 73 MB |

Language server path with gopls: server ready after 374 ms (paid once), go to definition 1.5 ms, find all references 3.0 ms, hover 5.1 ms, document outline 1.4 ms. px0 itself stays at 18 MB; gopls runs as a separate process at 122 MB.

Memory is returned to the OS after 15 seconds of inactivity. On the linux kernel, resident memory rises to 94 MB after searching and scrolling, then settles to 57 MB after 30 seconds idle.

## Architecture

- Single binary distribution: the web UI (~74 KB) is embedded with go:embed.
- In-memory path index with a bounded parallel directory walk (NumCPU x 4) and a specialized .gitignore engine.
- Git awareness and Myers diff engine: concurrent status scans and in-memory diffing against HEAD.
- Markdown rendering: goldmark GFM parser with Chroma syntax highlighter for code fences.
- Windowed syntax highlighting: 1,000-line chunks with 400 lines of context, a 512 KB window cap, and a 512 MB LRU cache of rendered HTML.
- Parallel search: whole-file rejection with bytes.Contains, per-worker buffer reuse, and in-place ASCII case folding. Results surface in the right inspector panel.
- Two-pass fuzzy matching in linear time, weighting consecutive runs, word boundaries, camelCase humps, and basename hits.
- Lazy LSP manager: servers are spawned on the first request for a language and shut down on exit.
- Agent dispatch runner: delegates edits to installed coding harnesses (Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Cursor Agent, Antigravity, OpenCode, Codex, Aider, Goose) with live streaming and auto-reload.
- Frontend DOM virtualization: about 60 live rows with 24 rows of overscan, painted inside requestAnimationFrame.

## Usage

```bash
px0                 # view the current workspace
px0 ~/src/kernel    # view another repository
px0 -host 0.0.0.0   # bind to all interfaces for remote browser access
px0 --update        # upgrade to the latest release
```

| Flag | Default | Description |
| ---- | ------- | ----------- |
| -port N | 7777 | Port to listen on (0 picks an ephemeral free port) |
| -host H | 127.0.0.1 | Local or remote address to bind (use 0.0.0.0 for remote access) |
| -no-open | false | Do not launch the web browser automatically |
| -no-lsp | false | Disable language server discovery and use regex-based outline |
| -no-git | false | Disable git awareness (tree status badges and diff view) |
| -agent H | none | Pin coding harness: claude, gemini, cursor-agent, agy, opencode, codex, aider, goose, or command template with {prompt} |
| -no-agent | false | Do not offer editing through a coding harness |
| -no-color | false | Strip ANSI escape sequences from terminal output |
| -quiet | false | Suppress CLI narration (errors still print to stderr) |
| -update | false | Check for updates and install the latest version |
| -version, -v | false | Print version and architecture and exit |

## Keyboard shortcuts

| Key | Action |
| --- | ------ |
| Cmd/Ctrl+K | Universal palette / quick open |
| Cmd/Ctrl+P | Go to file |
| Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+P | Command palette |
| Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+O | Go to symbol in file |
| Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+F | Full workspace search (opens right inspector tab) |
| Cmd/Ctrl+F | Find in active file |
| Cmd/Ctrl+D | Toggle git diff vs HEAD (split / unified) |
| Alt+M | Toggle rendered Markdown preview / source |
| Alt+E | Edit selected code with coding agent |
| F12, Cmd/Ctrl+Click | Go to definition |
| Shift+F12 | Find all references |
| Hover | Type signature and doc hover |
| Alt+Left / Alt+Right | Navigate back / forward in history |

The palette switches mode on its first character: `>` for commands, `@` for symbols, `:` for a line number, and no prefix for fuzzy file paths.

## Installation

Quick install (macOS, Linux, BSD):

```bash
curl -fsSL https://px0.ai/install.sh | sh
```

Prebuilt binaries for 15 OS and architecture combinations (darwin, linux, freebsd, openbsd, netbsd, windows) are on GitHub Releases.

From source (Go 1.24 or newer, no npm, no node, no CGO):

```bash
git clone https://github.com/px0-ai/px0.git
cd px0
make build
mkdir -p ~/.local/bin && install -m 755 px0 ~/.local/bin/px0
```
